::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[simple harmonic oscillator functions space and real plane](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1947973/simple-harmonic-oscillator-functions-space-and-real-plane), asked by [Arsh Gh](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/287583/arsh-gh) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-09-30; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> the functions that satisfy the simple harmonic oscillator equation
> $\frac{\mathrm{d}^2x  }{\mathrm{d} t^2}=-\omega _{0}^2x$
> constitute a linear space .
>
> is this linear space is isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^2$ ?
:::

This might be a bit advanced for you now, but eventually you may study linear systems of differential equations.  They take the form $\mathbf{y}'(t) = A \mathbf{y}(t)$, where $\mathbf{y}(t)$ is a (column) vector of $n$ functions of $t$, and $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix.  

Your equation is one of these, because you can let $y_1(t) = x(t)$ and $y_2(t) = x'(t)$.  Then $y_1' = y_2$ and $y_2' = -\omega_0^2 y_1$.  That is,
$$\begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \end{bmatrix}'
   =\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -\omega_0^2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}
    \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \end{bmatrix}$$

The solution space of a linear system of $n$ differential equations has dimension $n$.
